links.outcome: Ablation of extraction, ontology standardization, and prioritization modules on phenotyping performance
links.effect: Performance improved with the addition of each module, including ontology-grounded standardization to HPO terms; end-to-end ontology-based similarity 0.70 vs 0.58 for PhenoBERT.
links.quote: Ablation analyses demonstrated performance improvements with the addition of each module in RARE-PHENIX (extraction, standardization, and prioritization), supporting the value of modeling the full clinical phenotyping workflow.

unlisted_practices: Modeling the full clinical phenotyping workflow end-to-end rather than a single extraction task
Supervised ranking of diagnostically informative phenotypes

screen.reason: The study develops and retrospectively/externally benchmarks an end-to-end LLM-based phenotyping framework (RARE-PHENIX) against baselines and ablation variants on clinical notes, without evaluating a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
